clue.text: Welshman wrapping one leg around head of travelling preacher

indicators.note: wrapping says the Welsh surname is put round the next piece

parts.note: Evans is a typically Welsh surname, standing for a Welshman

indicators.note: around says the words one and leg are turned to run backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word travelling

explanation.surface: A Welshman bandaging a leg near the head of a wandering preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The Welsh surname wraps the reversed letters; the definition is just 'preacher', with 'travelling' lending only its first letter while colouring the picture of an itinerant preacher.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist is a preacher who tours, spreading the gospel from place to place.

clue.text: Reduce rent (20% off, initially)

indicators.note: off says letters are taken away, and initially says it is the opening one that goes

parts.note: to lease property is to rent it
one letter of a five-letter word is twenty percent of it

explanation.surface: A landlord cutting the rent by a fifth at the start of a tenancy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain or pressure is to lessen or relieve it.

clue.text: E.g. the skill independent learner retained in modern times

parts.note: art means skill or craft

indicators.note: retained in says one letter is held inside the abbreviation for modern times

parts.note: CE stands for Common Era, the modern dating period
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A grammar point: a self-taught learner keeping up a skill in the present day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E.g. the' is a definition by example: 'the' is the definite article in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the definite article, so it is an example of that word class.

clue.text: Strange clue about queen's cavalryman

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A puzzling hint concerning a monarch's mounted soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like the anagram signal but is itself fodder: both words are shuffled, with 'about' the signal, and the queen's letters follow.
explanation.definitionFit: George Armstrong Custer was a US cavalry commander, killed at the Little Bighorn in 1876.

clue.text: City worked up energy for game

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
worked up means angry, or cross
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A city angered by the energy spent on a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks.

clue.text: Portuguese saint riddled with 55 shots

indicators.note: riddled with says the saint's word is filled by the numeral

parts.note: São is Portuguese for saint, as in São Paulo
LV is 55 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A Portuguese saint's statue peppered with fifty-five bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst of gunfire, many shots fired together.

clue.text: German behind bar in South Africa is party animal

indicators.note: behind says the German letter comes after the rest
in says the bar's letter sits inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: SA is South Africa
T is a bar, as in a T-bar

explanation.surface: A German propping up a bar in South Africa is a real party-goer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party animal' looks like a reveller, but it is a pun: the stag at a stag party, the British name for a bachelor party.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, and it gives its name to the groom's night out before a wedding.

clue.text: Start of terrible hullabaloo in newspaper business

indicators.note: Start of picks the first letter of the word terrible
in says the noise goes inside the newspaper

parts.note: rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper
a din is a loud noise or hullabaloo

explanation.surface: A dreadful uproar breaks out in a newspaper office.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading is commerce, buying and selling as a line of work.

clue.text: Parasites manipulated feelings about religion

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the religion abbreviation
manipulated says the letters of feelings are worked into a new order

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: Bloodsuckers who play on people's emotions about faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parasites' sounds human in the surface, but these are the sap-sucking insects; 'about' signals that the jumbled letters go round the school-subject abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids feed by sucking sap from plants, so these green insects are plant parasites.

clue.text: Making comeback in cartoon? A Tasmanian devil!

indicators.note: Making comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cartoon Tasmanian devil, like Taz in Looney Tunes, returning to the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters sits inside 'cartoon? A Tasmanian'; 'in' points to it being hidden there.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is the Devil of Christian scripture, so the lower-case devil fits.

clue.text: A London vagrant sheltering in church portico

indicators.note: sheltering says the church letters hold the jumbled words inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: vagrant means wandering, so these letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A homeless Londoner sleeping in a church porch.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonnade is a row of columns, as along a porch or portico.

clue.text: Meerkat ran her ragged, to be more precise

indicators.note: running someone ragged suggests disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A meerkat chased a woman until she was exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being closer to the target means more accurate, an idiom from aiming.

clue.text: Further evidence Robert is replacing Penny in council

indicators.note: is replacing says the name's short form takes the coin letter's place

parts.note: a corporation is a town or city council
P is for penny in British money
Rob is short for Robert

explanation.surface: Proof that a councillor named Robert has been swapped in for a woman called Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name, but it is the coin abbreviation P.
explanation.definitionFit: Corroboration is confirming evidence that backs up an existing claim.

clue.text: Surprising fact about Victor and Joy

parts.note: re means about or concerning
V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet
elation is great joy

explanation.surface: A shock disclosure involving two people named Victor and Joy.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation is an eye-opening disclosure, something unexpected made known.

clue.text: Old version of The Mirror put on electronic viewing device

indicators.note: put on says the following letters come after the electronic letter

parts.note: E is short for electronic, as in e-mail
ye is an archaic form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe
a glass is a mirror, as in looking glass

explanation.surface: An old edition of The Mirror newspaper is put onto an e-reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Mirror' looks like the British tabloid, but 'The' and 'Mirror' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle or single lens worn to aid sight is an aid to vision.

clue.text: Mountain trail twisting round historic Indian province

parts.note: Ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: twisting round says the word for falling behind is turned backwards

parts.note: to trail is to lag behind

explanation.surface: A mountain path winding through an old region of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengal was a province of British India, now split between India and Bangladesh.

clue.text: Show fellow setter heartless editorials in newspaper

parts.note: a man is a fellow
the setter refers to themself as I

indicators.note: in says the trimmed word goes inside the newspaper's initials

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times

indicators.note: heartless removes everything but the first and last letters of editorials

explanation.surface: A man shows the crossword setter some soulless newspaper leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: To manifest is to display or make evident, a verb meaning to show.

clue.text: Former love meets American aboard Delta flight

indicators.note: aboard says the American letters get on next to the Delta letter

parts.note: ex means former
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
D is Delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An ex-partner bumps into an American on a Delta Air Lines plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like air travel, fitting Delta the airline; it is fleeing, as in the Exodus of the Israelites from Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: An exodus is a mass departure, people fleeing a place together.

clue.text: Circular part of drill used in test

indicators.note: used in says the drill part goes inside the exam word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
the bit is the cutting part of a drill

explanation.surface: A round drill bit being tested.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbital means going round in a ring, like a ring road or a path around a planet.

clue.text: Haul crone before cardinal — an enemy of Rome

parts.note: to cart is to haul
a hag is an ugly old woman
E, east, is a cardinal point of the compass

explanation.surface: Dragging an old witch before a church cardinal, an opponent of the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman, which fits 'Rome'; it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage, the north African city-state, fought Rome in the Punic Wars.

clue.text: Fool English soldier, concealing a weapon

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: concealing says the soldier's letters hide the next letter inside them

parts.note: GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: An idiot English soldier hiding a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Barnier's art is misconstrued as inconsistency

indicators.note: misconstrued means wrongly interpreted, so the letters are read into a new order

explanation.surface: Michel Barnier, the EU's Brexit negotiator, has his artistry dismissed as erratic.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbitrariness is acting on whim without consistent rules or reasons.

clue.text: Use a mask, we are told

indicators.note: we are told signals that the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: a veil is a mask covering the face

explanation.surface: Instructions to wear a face covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means benefit or use, as in to no avail.

clue.text: Beat fellow with lump of wood

parts.note: F is short for fellow, as in FRS
a log is a lump of wood

explanation.surface: Hitting a man with a club.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is to whip or thrash someone.

clue.text: Worry about taking expert on in meeting

indicators.note: taking, as in taking on, says the expert word is added after the worry word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about says the worry word is turned backwards

parts.note: to fret is to worry
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Fretting over bringing in a specialist for a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An interface is a point where two systems or parties meet and interact.

clue.text: Divine creature felt naked beside knight clad in silver

indicators.note: beside says the two parts sit next to each other
clad in says the knight's letter is dressed in the silver symbol

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: naked strips off the outer letters of felt

explanation.surface: A heavenly being felt bare next to a knight in silver armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Angels are heavenly beings, messengers of God.

clue.text: Flower girl regularly seen in Tyneside

indicators.note: seen in says the picked letters go inside the region's letters

parts.note: NE stands for the North East of England, where Tyneside is

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of girl, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A flower girl spotted from time to time around Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword trick for a river: something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, and the Nile is the great African river.

clue.text: Attack Great Britain about importing Ritz-like crackers

indicators.note: importing says the jumbled letters are brought inside
about says the country's letters are turned round

parts.note: GB is Great Britain

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: An assault on Britain using imported crackers like Ritz biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: A blitzkrieg is a sudden, intense military offensive, German for lightning war.
